Callers then use the result with provider-specific assumptions: Google's CalendarService does `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token` — a fetch Response has no `.data`, so sharing mode breaks. judged_text: refreshOAuthTokens returns incompatible shapes between modes: in sharing mode it returns a raw fetch Response while callers expect their provider's return type (Google expects gaxios res.data so token.access_token throws TypeError, Hubspot expects a parsed token object so undefined tokens and NaN expiry get persisted, Zoho Bigin/CRM expect axios responses so tokenInfo.data.error throws), and Lark/O365/Webex/Zoom only work if the endpoint mimics each provider's exact response envelope, contradicting the function's documented contract
